item.title: On the Performance of Randomly Generated Codebooks in Near-Field Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.12588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-field communication with large antenna arrays requires beamforming techniques that account for spherical wavefront effects. While predefined codebooks are widely used in multiple-antenna wireless systems, the performance of randomly generated codebooks in the near-field region has not been investigated. In this work, we study four randomly generated codebooks for near-field communications: random vector quantization (RVQ), random phase (RP), random far-field (RFF), and random near-field (RNF) codebooks. We use the known RVQ gain distribution as a benchmark. For RP, we derive a large-array bulk approximation and characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RNF, we characterize the high-gain tail behavior of the gain distribution. For RFF, we derive an analytical approximation for the maximum achievable beamforming gain when far-field beams are used to serve near-field users, along with the corresponding maximizing far-field direction. We also analyze the maximum-gain scaling with codebook size. Monte Carlo simulations verify the analytical results and show that RVQ and RP degrade significantly as the array size increases, while RNF achieves the most favorable high-gain scaling. RFF can outperform RVQ and RP for finite codebook sizes, but its maximum gain saturates below one due to the phase mismatch between the far-field beams and the near-field channel. These results show how codebook structure, array size, and codebook size affect random beamforming performance in the near-field.
item.dc:creator: Akarsh Yadav, Ly V. Nguyen, James V. Krogmeier, David J. Love

item.title: Simultaneous Direct and Indirect Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted MIMO Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.12592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces an enhanced channel estimation method for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. Considering the presence of both the direct link from the base station (BS) to the user equipment (UE) and the indirect link \textit{via} the RIS, we formulate a tensor-based receiver for joint direct and indirect channel estimation called the TenDICE algorithm. The proposed receiver relies on an extended parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) tensor model for the received pilot signals, from which the involved (direct and indirect link) channels are estimated using a simple alternating least squares scheme. The proposed TenDICE method is compared with the state-of-the-art least squares (LS) method, Khatri-Rao factorization (KRF) method, enhanced trilinear alternating least squares (E-TALS), and the theoretical Cram\'er-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based on normalized mean square error (NMSE) and spectral efficiency (SE). The proposed TenDICE outperforms the LS and E-TALS methods and performs similarly to the KRF methods while estimating the direct channel.
item.dc:creator: Daniel V. C. de Oliveira, Daniel C. Alcantara, Fazal. E Asim, Andre L. F. de Almeida, Gabor Fodor

item.title: Low-Complexity Tensor-Based Channel Parameter Estimation for mmWave MIMO-Assisted Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.12604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a low-complexity tensor-based channel estimation framework for downlink mmWave massive MIMO systems using passive Butler-matrix beamforming. By modeling received signals as a third-order PARAFAC tensor, we exploit known pilot structures via bilinear alternating least-squares (BALS) optimization to reduce computational overhead. The decoupled spatial factors are then processed via 1D and 2D ESPRIT to extract angles of arrival and departure with automatic pairing. Additionally, we derive the Cramer--Rao lower bound (CRLB) for this architecture. Simulations confirm the proposed estimator outperforms conventional least-squares, achieving accurate channel reconstruction and approaching the CRLB at moderate-to-high signal-to-noise ratios.
item.dc:creator: Francisco I. T. Pires, Jean C. S. Ferreira, Fazal-E Asim

item.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
item.description: arXiv:2610.12686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.
item.dc:creator: Ralph Kumah Assan, Suresh Singh

item.title: Generative Control of Time-Modulated Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Scalable Directional Modulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.12773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-modulated intelligent reflecting surfaces (TM-IRS) achieve directional modulation by switching their elements on and off at designed instants and durations, so that an undistorted signal reaches the intended user while appearing scrambled elsewhere. We propose a Flow Matching (FM)-based generative framework that designs these parameters for strong scrambling and reliable reception simultaneously. For orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, we introduce a physics-informed reward that maximizes the time-modulation harmonic energy radiated in the null space of the legitimate-user response, subject to a minimum per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR), without requiring knowledge of adversary directions. Unlike prior generative flow network (GFlowNet) approaches, which assign discretized parameters sequentially, the FM model generates complete continuous configurations jointly, decoupling the generation depth from the number of elements and accelerating training. It also learns a distribution over configurations that can be resampled to vary the scrambling pattern. Numerical results show that, compared with a GFlowNet baseline, the proposed approach reduces the time to training loss near-saturation by $99.4\%$ on average for $3{\times}3$ to $12{\times}12$ surfaces, attains higher final rewards, scales to $80{\times}80$, and confines the low-symbol-error region more tightly around the legitimate user.
item.dc:creator: Kailong Wang, Sida Xiang, Athina Petropulu

item.title: Self-Calibration DOA Estimation for Moving Dilated Arrays with Gain and Phase Errors
item.description: arXiv:2610.12934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moving dilated arrays (MDAs) can increase the uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs) while alleviating mutual coupling, but their performance is susceptible to unknown gain and phase errors (GPEs). To deal with this problem, we investigate self-calibration direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for MDAs with unknown GPEs. First, multi-position observations are phase aligned to construct an equivalent virtual array with an enlarged aperture. Next, the motion-induced relationships among the GPEs are exploited to establish explicit calibration constraints. By leveraging the orthogonality between the steering vectors and the noise subspace, the joint estimation of the DOAs and GPEs is formulated as a constrained optimization problem. To solve this problem, a two-stage alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is developed. In the first stage, the GPEs are estimated in closed form with the DOAs fixed. In the second stage, the estimated GPEs are used to calibrate the covariance matrix, after which the DOAs are refined using the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To obtain reliable initial estimates, a rotational invariance-like (RIL) initialization method is further developed by exploiting two translated virtual subarrays with identical GPEs. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the theoretical performance limit of the considered system. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges reliably and achieves accurate DOA estimation under different array apertures, numbers of snapshots, GPE levels, and numbers of sources.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyuan Fang, Chengzhi Ye, Ruoyu Zhang, Shichao Wei, Wen Wu

item.title: Lightweight Time-Frequency Vibration Sensing for Consumer Device Condition Monitoring
item.description: arXiv:2610.13040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consumer rotating devices, including washing machines, air conditioners, electric fans, robotic vacuum cleaners, and home fitness equipment, increasingly rely on vibration sensing for intelligent condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Ensuring reliable operation in these resource-constrained appliances requires efficient, lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) solutions capable of processing non-stationary signals under real-world operational interference. This paper proposes a lightweight AI-assisted vibration sensing framework that employs continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) to convert one-dimensional (1-D) vibration time-series signals into two-dimensional (2-D) time-frequency representations. These representations are subsequently analyzed using lightweight deep learning architectures, specifically MobileNetV3-Small, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and the You Only Look Once version 11 classification model (YOLOv11-cls). Public bearing benchmark datasets, including Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), and Intelligent Maintenance Systems (IMS), are utilized as representative rotating components to investigate model generalization. The proposed framework is designed with eventual embedded deployment in consumer electronics in mind. Experimental results demonstrate that CWT combined with YOLOv11-cls achieves high diagnostic accuracy, while MobileNetV3-Small provides an attractive low-latency alternative for computationally constrained edge platforms. Conventional random splitting is also compared with dataset-specific structured isolation. The results highlight the importance of avoiding data leakage and quantify tradeoffs in classification accuracy, parameter count, floating-point operations (FLOPs), model footprint, preprocessing cost, and central processing unit (CPU) inference latency.
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Jen-Yu Chiu, Chun-Yu Yeh, Wei-Lung Mao, Walid Saad

item.title: Certified Outage Dimensioning of Fluid Antenna Receivers: Required SNR, Aperture, and Port Count
item.description: arXiv:2610.13094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the SNR, aperture, and port count needed to meet a target outage in a single-user downlink with a fixed transmit antenna and a single-RF fluid antenna receiver. For known spatially correlated Rayleigh channels and ideal port selection, a sampling-free residual certificate controls reduced-rank outage error over a continuous SNR interval. Positive Bessel features support large arrays, and bounded importance sampling converts the certificate into simultaneous design intervals. At 1 bit/s/Hz and outage $10^{-5}$, a four-wavelength, ten-port receiver requires 4.40--4.55 dB. Reducing its port count from 256 to ten costs 0.70--1.25 dB under a joint 95\% probability statement. At 3.5 wavelengths, ten ports require 4.90--5.05 dB. Integer-port screening across 3--8 dB shows how aperture and port requirements change with available SNR; an effective-SNR transformation extends these decisions to other rates. The reported intervals include model and sampling uncertainty under checked Gaussian covariance inputs. A constructive slow-growth rank bound and a 16--1024-port study support compact evaluation as port count grows.
item.dc:creator: Yuanjun Shen

item.title: LLM-Assisted Hierarchical Interference Control for Satellite-Terrestrial Integrated Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.13108v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-varying aggregate interference from low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites challenges terrestrial-network (TN) protection, whereas conservative control degrades LEO quality of service (QoS). This letter proposes a hierarchical framework combining geometry-based interference estimation, QoS-constrained power control, adaptive energy detection, large language model (LLM)-assisted candidate ranking, stay-or-switch decisions, and target-band selection, with deterministic verification. The current band is retained only when both spectrum-hole and power-feasibility conditions hold, with periodic reevaluation. Over a 300-s horizon with 0.5-s sampling, the proposed method keeps the aggregate INR from exceeding the $-12.2$~dB threshold and achieves a time-averaged mean LEO-link rate of $320.97$~Mbps with $100\%$ QoS satisfaction. It markedly outperforms power-only and satellite-muting in jointly protecting the TN and preserving LEO QoS.
item.dc:creator: Heying Cao, Hao Yuan, Xing Zhang

item.title: JEPA-kMMVAE: CSI Prediction for Time-Varying Wireless Channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.13315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers channel state information (CSI) prediction using neural networks for time-varying multi-antenna channels from noisy historical observations. The main challenge is to exploit temporal correlation while distinguishing channel evolution from observation noise. We propose JEPA-kMMVAE, which combines a joint-embedding predictive architecture with a k-memory Markov variational autoencoder to predict future CSI through temporally structured latent representations. The framework supports direct prediction and residual corrections relative to the latest latent state and noisy CSI observation. Simulation results show that the residual configuration outperforms the evaluated baselines at moderate and high input CSI signal-to-noise ratios, while sequence baselines remain more accurate under stronger noise.
item.dc:creator: Efstathios Chatziloizos, Konstantinos Vandikas, Aneta Vulgarakis Feljan, Zheng Chen, Nikolaos Pappas

item.title: Towards Signal Processing In Networks: Multiplierless Block Transforms in Data Plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.13324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a signal processing concept, signal processing in networks (SPIN), that executes signal processing tasks directly on programmable switches. Traditionally, signal processing tasks, such as denoising, decomposition, and dimensionality reduction, are performed on edge or cloud servers, i.e., raw streams are transmitted from sensors. This imposes a heavy processing load on edge/cloud servers and requires substantial bandwidth. SPIN addresses this problem by performing signal processing on the forwarding path. As an initial realization of SPIN, we implement a DCT-based block transform on a programmable switch. We redesign its computation using a lifting-based lattice structure, multiplierless approximation, and pipeline partitioning across stages in a programmable switch. We verify at the compiler level that the proposed implementation satisfies the strict hardware constraints of the Intel Tofino2--specifically regarding pipeline stages, packet header vector, and ternary content-addressable memory usage--and therefore enables line-rate processing. We further quantify the per-packet latency of the ingress match-action pipeline. The SPIN-oriented preprocessing adds 46 cycles (approximately 31 ns at 1.5 GHz). The total ingress match-action unit latency is approximately 87 ns, which remains consistent with the low-latency operation targeted by SPIN. Furthermore, we implement the proposed block transform on a BMv2 switch using P4 and evaluate it as preprocessing for in-network machine learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves classification performance over unfiltered baselines.
item.dc:creator: Shota Ono, Marika Morikawa, Kazuma Kaneko, Junya Hara, Hiroshi Higashi, Shigenori Tani, Yuichi Tanaka

item.title: Scalable Quantum Clustering of Renewable Profiles via a Hybrid Qubit-efficient Strategy
item.description: arXiv:2610.13336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale renewable energy profile clustering is a computationally challenging NP-hard problem. Recent quantum computing techniques offer a potential remedy, yet their scalability is severely constrained by the limited qubit count of current quantum hardware. To address this issue, we first cast the problem into a QUBO form and then we propose a consensus-based variable reduction (CBVR) method to drastically cut qubit usage. More specifically, we tailor the one-hot constraint to eliminate assignment variables and leverage consensus analysis to convert stable clustering relations from initial anneals into equality constraints for further reduction. Experiments on real quantum hardware confirm that CBVR compresses oversized QUBO models into feasible sizes while retaining high clustering quality and efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Cao, Chengjun Liu, Yijun Xu, Kai Wen, Wei Gu, Lamine Mili, Shuai Lu

item.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
item.description: arXiv:2610.13357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure transmission of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains a major challenge in telecardiology. While traditional mathematical watermarking can embed patient metadata directly into ECG signals, it is highly fragile against temporal desynchronization such as circular phase shifts. In contrast, existing deep watermarking approaches for temporal signals, such as audio, typically rely on lossy quantization, which compromises the high-frequency micro-morphological details critical for clinical diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we propose ECGWmark, a fully convolutional and quantization-free deep watermarking framework for medical time-series. ECGWmark operates in a continuous, full-resolution latent space and utilizes a localized frame-level mechanism to improve the robustness to severe desynchronization. Crucially, we introduce a differentiable Physiological Loss guided by a clinical classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Experiments on the benchmark MIT-BIH database show that ECGWmark maintains channel-bit extraction accuracy above 90% under the evaluated circular temporal shifts. Furthermore, under a rigorous inter-patient diagnostic evaluation, Class-V sensitivity changes from 71.97% to 76.50%, whereas Macro-F1 changes from 35.25% to 34.71% and Class-S sensitivity from 8.89% to 1.39%; these results indicate mixed class-level effects.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Yu Chen, Kuan-Chen Wang, Yu Tsao, Jian-Jiun Ding

item.title: Tri-Hybrid SWIPT with Reconfigurable Parasitic Antennas
item.description: arXiv:2610.13402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a coupling-aware tri-hybrid precoding architecture for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) using reconfigurable parasitic antennas. By integrating multiport network theory and information theory, we develop a third precoding layer that explicitly accounts for mutual coupling and reactive energy storage within the antenna domain. To efficiently optimize this architecture, we propose a low-complexity tri-hybrid solution comprising coordinate descent (CD) for parasitic reactive load optimization, a singular value decomposition (SVD)-based analog precoder, and a protective partial zero-forcing (PPZF) digital precoder. Numerical results demonstrate that the transmit array introduces impedance mismatch that reduces the real power accepted by the antenna array. Moreover, the proposed tri-hybrid architecture significantly outperforms hybrid precoding by constructively exploiting the coupling effects, yielding substantial gains in spectral efficiency (SE) and sum non-linear harvested energy (NLHE) at a fraction of the hardware cost.
item.dc:creator: Thien Duc Hua, Mohammadali Mohammadi, Hien Quoc Ngo, Michail Matthaiou

item.title: One Thing Leads to Another: The Essentials of Time Series Causal Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2610.13430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time series causal discovery --- the process of detecting causation between time series --- has its roots in signal processing research from over a half century ago. It has since received active and widespread interest, evolving into different forms across domains such as statistics, dynamical systems and machine learning. Entering this fragmented and constantly evolving research landscape can be daunting. This tutorial provides a unified overview of time series causal discovery across research communities. We introduce the key principles invoked by modern discovery methods, and we discuss their limitations and assumptions. We also discuss how discovery methods are evaluated, benchmarked and fine-tuned. We further discuss how causal discovery for time series is becoming crucial for downstream tasks in agriculture and Earth science, in healthcare, and in artificial intelligence systems. We believe that this tutorial will serve as a valuable resource in navigating the deluge of recent causality research, as well as an invitation to signal processing audiences to contribute to causal problems. To further help readers, we host a companion repository to link to useful code packages and resources at https://github.com/CHAI-UK/Awesome-Time-Series-Causal-Discovery.
item.dc:creator: Kurt Butler, Damian Machlanski, Michael P. J. Camilleri, Zhihua Liu, Panagiotis Dimitrakopoulos, Feng Chen, Ricardo Silva, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris

item.title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the grid quantization error of deep-learning (DL)-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Classification- based DOA methods discretize the continuous angular space into a grid, so that with a peak-based read-out, the accuracy and resolution are limited by the grid step and by the width of the label peak. To address this issue, we propose a sigmoid label that encodes the sources' DOAs as the sum of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the output of a CNN-Transformer network trained with the sigmoid label produces sharp spectral peaks at the source DOAs. Combined with a moderately refined grid step of 0.25 degrees, the CNN-Transformer with the proposed sigmoid label attains sub-degree accuracy and a 1-degree resolution, breaking the limit of the grid quantization error. Under the unified CNN-Transformer backbone, we compare the proposed Sigmoid label with the Gaussian label, the 0-1 hard label, and the binary cross-entropy (BCE) baseline. Numerical results demonstrate that the Sigmoid label attains the highest accuracy and superior resolution compared to other labels.
item.dc:creator: Lifeng Wang, Xintong Li, Aifei Liu

item.title: Blind and Asynchronous Initial Beam Acquisition and Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition in Standalone Mobile MIMO-OFDM Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building upon our preliminary study, this paper proposes a standalone beam-management framework for mobile MIMO-OFDM systems that integrates Blind Initial Beam Acquisition (BIBA) with Clock-Assisted Re-Acquisition (CARA). BIBA is a blind and asynchronous protocol that requires neither prior synchronization nor an out-of-band feedback channel, so the Base Station (BS) and User Equipment (UE) can independently identify the beam pair maximizing received signal strength. To handle subsequent link drops, the newly introduced CARA protocol exploits the clock synchronization established after BIBA to reduce the re-acquisition time by approximately 55% compared with BIBA. The operational reliability of both protocols is bounded by a probabilistic feasibility analysis under random UE mobility trajectories. Protocols are validated on a 28 GHz mmWave testbed under practical hardware constraints, including beam-switching and Time Division Duplex (TDD) latencies, and measured Software-Defined Radio (SDR) software processing delays. Finally, we formulate a unified Finite State Machine (FSM) model for both BIBA and CARA to ensure robust integration into practical wireless systems
item.dc:creator: Ali Abdi, Firooz B. Saghezchi, Haris Gacanin

item.title: Suppressing Multiple GNSS Interferers with Local-Gradient Adaptive Notch Filtering
item.description: arXiv:2610.13443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive notch filters (ANFs) based on the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm are an established technique for suppressing narrowband interference in GNSS receivers. The traditional solution for multiple interferers is simply cascading the NLMS-ANF into multiple stages but this solution degrades performance when multiple chirp jammers of similar power are present. We propose a low-complexity modification to the cascaded NLMS-ANF update rule to resolve this: a local gradient (LG) formulation: LG-ANF. The LG-ANF forms a locally bandlimited gradient signal by translating the input to baseband around the current frequency estimate, low-pass filtering it, and translating it back, thereby attenuating competing interferers before adaptation. The modification generalizes the traditional NLMS-ANF to handle the similar-power multiple interferer problem, using just one additional parameter. We characterize the gradient-averaging failure analytically and visually, demonstrate independent chirp tracking in the worst-case two-chirp scenarios, and evaluate statistical suppression performance by sweeping amplitude ratio against a standard NLMS-ANF, a frequency-locked-loop (FLL)-based ANF and a per-sample oracle upper bound. We further characterize the LG advantage over various ANF parameters and chirp conditions. Simulations show that the LG-ANF reduces to the standard NLMS-ANF outside the pathological multi-chirp regime, while recovering up to 4dB of in-band suppression around pathological amplitude ratios under per-condition optimization of the local bandwidth, and up to 13dB for selected edge-case parameter combinations. These optimized results represent an upper bound on the achievable LG gain. In a hardware experiment using a fixed alpha_lp=0.5, the LG-ANF extends position-lock survival by 24s relative to the standard ANF.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proc. of the Intl. Technical Meeting of the Satellite Division of the Institute of Navigation (ION GNSS+), pages 672-683, Orlando, FL, September 2026
item.dc:creator: Burak Soner, Felix Ott

item.title: HF Single-Station Localization via Multimode Ray Tracing and Time-Frequency Information Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.13560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-frequency (HF) single-station localization estimates an emitter location from measured directions of arrival (DOAs) and an ionospheric propagation model. When the propagation mode composition cannot be identified from conventional direction-finding (DF) measurements, the same DF observation may produce multiple physically valid ground landing points under different propagation modes, making the location inversion ambiguous. This paper proposes a multimode time-frequency information fusion localization method (MTFIF-L).Rather than assuming a propagation mode a priori, MTFIF-L retains valid landing points generated under different propagation modes and uses repeated observations across time windows and, when available, multiple operating frequencies to progressively constrain the resulting candidate locations. Experiments on four measured HF links examine the respective roles of multimode candidate retention, cross-window processing, and cross-frequency processing. All four links yield unique location decisions. Links A--C achieve relative errors of $1.40\%$, $0.78\%$, and $3.41\%$, respectively.Link D, the only single-frequency case, also yields a unique decision from repeated temporal observations, although its post- localization error is substantially larger. Propagation-path analysis further reveals link-dependent differences in reflection layer, hop count, magnetoionic mode, and elevation angle among the ray-tracing paths associated with the measured links.Overall, the results show that repeated temporal observations can support localization within an individual frequency, while multifrequency information provides additional robustness against unreliable frequency-specific outcomes, enabling HF single-station localization under unknown and potentially coexisting propagation modes while retaining interpretable propagation information for post-localization analysis.
item.dc:creator: Qinglin Li, Wen Liu, Yun Ning, Zhongxin Deng, Junkang He, Mingshuo Liu, Chuangjian Xia

item.title: OpenH-RF: A Large-Scale Ultrasound Raw Channel Dataset Initiative
item.description: arXiv:2610.13616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical ultrasound is a widely accessible, real-time imaging modality, yet progress in data-driven ultrasound research is constrained by the scarcity of large, open collections of raw channel data. Existing public datasets are predominantly based on reconstructed images, while the smaller number of open raw channel datasets is generally specialized to individual reconstruction or imaging tasks, limiting the development of general-purpose methods and foundation models that operate directly on ultrasound signals. While interpretive tasks can be performed on reconstructed images, many of the key technical challenges in ultrasound imaging, such as aberration correction and reverberation reduction, require the raw channel data itself. We introduce OpenH-RF, a community-driven open dataset initiative comprising approximately 40 TB of medical ultrasound raw channel data in 19,332 acquisitions, contributed by 38 institutions across academia and industry, spanning in-vivo, phantom, and simulated data. Each dataset is annotated with a number of supported tasks, ranging from generalized reconstruction, speed-of-sound estimation, and aberration correction to blood flow imaging, motion estimation, quantitative ultrasound, and image interpretation. OpenH-RF provides a unified, self-contained data format that captures raw channel data together with the acquisition, probe, metadata, and reconstruction information required for reproducible processing across scanners and acquisition schemes. The corpus is publicly hosted under a permissive CC BY 4.0 license and can be streamed programmatically and selectively at scale. By bringing heterogeneous ultrasound data into a common representation, backed by modern data infrastructure, OpenH-RF lowers the barrier to working with raw channel data and aims to open medical ultrasound research to new communities. See https://open-h.github.io/OpenH-RF.

item.title: EarLog: Opportunistic Ear Physiology Sensing toward Personalized Hearing Risk Awareness
item.description: arXiv:2610.12501v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many headphone users risk irreversible hearing damage during high-load listening, yet current protection still relies on sound-pressure limits. Clinical tests detect damage after it becomes measurable, leaving the risk-accumulating process unobserved. The acoustic reflex (AR), an involuntary response to high acoustic load, marks when the ear enters a protective state. AR traces are weak, and existing measurements require dedicated probes and controlled conditions that are difficult to maintain during everyday audio. We present EarLog, which turns playback, the dominant interference, into an opportunistic probe. EarLog introduces content-conditioned residual sensing to suppress variations caused by nonstationary content, individual ear acoustics, and device response. It identifies weak AR through loudness-dependent changes and localized spectral irregularities in the residual. A resonance-constrained sparse finite impulse response (FIR) model captures the short-window response. Dual-microphone observations, mild-distortion recovery, and cross-session reference updates keep detection usable under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), fit changes, and environmental drift. EarLog runs in real time on an embedded controller using a low-cost dual-microphone add-on. We evaluate it with 81 participants, 16 headphone models, and more than 400 hours of recordings. EarLog achieves 99.0% sensitivity and 98.7% specificity on a clinically referenced benchmark. EarLog records listener-specific AR events during everyday listening, providing data for future longitudinal studies of hearing risk.
item.dc:creator: Yongzhi Huang, Jiayi Zhao, Kaishun Wu

item.title: Expert-level detection of low-voltage intervals in EEG as a robust biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background: Discontinuity in neonatal EEG is a critical marker of brain dysfunction but can be difficult to quantify visually. Inter-burst intervals (IBIs) are a key characteristic of discontinuity, yet their definition does not easily translate to AI detection. Objectives: To introduce low-voltage intervals (LVIs), defined exclusively by amplitude and duration, as a context-independent alternative to IBIs, develop an AI detection method for LVIs, and assess their clinical utility as a marker of brain injury. Methods: We developed a ConvNeXt model to detect LVIs and compared its performance with existing methods. We then tested the clinical relevance of detected LVIs across four applications: 1) grading background EEG abnormalities on an open benchmark dataset, 2) classifying clinical hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) grades and comparing with a normal EEG dataset, 3) seizure prediction, and 4) association with seizure burden. Results: For training and validation, 654 hours of per-channel EEG from 123 neonates were reviewed and 51,162 LVIs were annotated. On held-out validation, ConvNeXt had an AUC of 0.996 and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.926. Model-reader agreement exceeded inter-reader agreement ($\Delta \kappa = 0.025$, 95% CI: 0.007 to 0.045, $p<0.001$), attaining expert-level equivalence. On a combined dataset of 444 neonates, percentage LVI showed a strong association with EEG grades (Spearman's $\rho=0.801$), a moderate association with HIE grades ($\rho=0.384$), a weaker association with seizure burden ($\rho=0.244$), and a strong seizure prediction capacity (AUC $=0.872$). Conclusion: AI detection of LVIs achieves expert-level equivalence, whereas quantitative features do not. Automated LVI quantification provides a robust clinical biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy associated with background EEG activity, HIE severity, and seizure risk.
item.dc:creator: John M. O'Toole, Sean R. Mathieson, Aurel Luca, Soraia Ventura, Sean Griffin, Geraldine B. Boylan, Robert Hogan

item.title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders
item.description: arXiv:2610.12820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The shock response spectrum (SRS) characterizes the peak responses of single-degree-of-freedom systems to transient acceleration. Because the mapping from an acceleration time series (waveform) to its SRS is many-to-one, inverse synthesis seeks candidate waveforms consistent with a prescribed spectrum. We extend an earlier conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) framework with a recurrent decoder that predicts multiscale wavelet coefficients and reconstructs waveforms through an inverse discrete wavelet transform. Individual models exhibit limited variability under latent sampling, motivating an ensemble of independently trained models spanning different mother wavelets and decomposition levels. Each member produces a separate candidate waveform for the same target SRS. Evaluation on four held-out benchmark datasets shows lower mean and median spectral errors for the illustrated wavelet model than for the earlier direct time-domain CVAE and a sum-of-decayed-sinusoids (SDS) baseline. A conditioning study examines frequency-grid and encoding choices. Comparisons with published inverse-SRS methods demonstrate superior performance across four holdout benchmark datasets (two operational shock datasets, one earthquake dataset, and one synthetic shock dataset) and competitive performance on synthetic targets reported by Brake. Single-model inference requires approximately 0.1-0.6 ms per waveform during batched inference compared with 5-8 s for SDS, excluding offline training. This low inference cost enables rapid generation of distinct SRS-compatible candidate waveforms across the ensemble, although their physical suitability requires assessment beyond spectral agreement.
item.dc:creator: Adam Watts, Charles Young, Ryan Bowering, Andrew Jeon, Destry Newton

item.title: Stochastic Finite-Transition Learning and Exploration for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2610.13095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative MRI reconstruction maps an initial source distribution to the target image distribution along a learned recovery trajectory. Common generative methods, such as diffusion and flow, typically learn fine-grained local dynamics whose integration defines this global mapping, hence requiring many network evaluations at inference. Existing few-step sampling approaches can lower computational burden by approximating large transformations from local dynamics, albeit at the expense of reconstruction fidelity. FLEX-MRI instead partitions recovery into a small number of finite intervals between retained states defined by progressive changes in k-space support, and directly learns the reconstruction change across each interval. Because such finite transitions can admit multiple plausible outcomes, FLEX-MRI combines support-relaxed finite-transition learning with stochastic exploration. During training, randomized k-space sampling masks define finite-transition targets with varying support, while the prediction loss remains unrestricted by each individual mask. At inference, FLEX-MRI perturbs a random subset of currently estimated k-space coefficients, allowing the learned predictor to stochastically explore alternative transition paths. Each predicted state is then reconciled with the acquired measurements through data consistency. We theoretically show that this stochastic exploration induces nonzero transition-level variation through the learned recovery map and data consistency without requiring an auxiliary generative sampler. Experiments on multi-coil MRI datasets show that FLEX-MRI outperforms competing methods while maintaining computational efficiency comparable to few-step baselines.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Usama Mirza, Esin \"Ozt\"urk I\c{s}{\i}k, Tolga \c{C}ukur

item.title: Secrets in Preamble: Practical and Robust PHY Information Hiding for Wi-Fi
item.description: arXiv:2610.13367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physical layer (PHY) information hiding refers to the concealment of secrets within PHY waveforms without compromising the integrity of the primary communication link, thereby enabling critical applications such as covert communication, PHY steganography, and watermarking. The widespread deployment of Wi-Fi has motivated substantial research interest in hiding secrets within Wi-Fi waveforms. However, existing Wi-Fi information hiding approaches suffer from two limitations: restricted steganographic capacity and insufficient robustness against environmental variations, both of which severely constrain practical deployment. This work proposes to embed secrets within the Wi-Fi legacy short training field (L-STF). The designed method preserves the autocorrelation properties of Wi-Fi L-STF, ensuring that packet detection and coarse frequency offset compensation functionalities remain uncompromised. The secret embedding and extraction processes employ a pair of neural networks designed to learn optimal embedding rules and maximize steganographic capacity. We developed a prototype system and conducted comprehensive experiments across both indoor and outdoor environments. Experimental results show that our method can reliably embed 46 secret bits within Wi-Fi packets across diverse channel conditions, achieving significantly enhanced steganographic capacity and environmental robustness. The hardware prototype study validates the feasibility of the proposed Wi-Fi information hiding scheme.
item.dc:creator: Rui Pan, Guanxiong Shen, Linning Peng, Xinyu Qi, Junqing Zhang

item.title: Zeros of the Spectrogram of White Noise with Hermite Windows
item.description: arXiv:2610.13531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the zeros of the spectrogram of complex white noise analyzed with Hermite windows of order n, extending the classical Gaussian-window correspondence with Gaussian Analytic Functions to the polyanalytic setting. Using the polyanalytic Bargmann transform, these zeros split into two families according to the sign of the local Jacobian, giving rise to a natural notion of charge, and we show that these zeros are almost surely simple, isolated, and form a translation and rotation-invariant point process. We derive closed-form expressions for the one-point intensity, decomposed by charge, and also for the unsigned, signed, and hybrid two-point intensities. Besides, we prove that unlike the total repulsion observed with a Gaussian window, the Hermite window of order n generates a pair correlation function that converges at the origin to a strictly positive constant depending on n. Finally, we propose a numerical method for detecting spectrogram zeros via the winding number around candidate local minima.
item.dc:creator: Charaf Bellourak (LJK, DAO), Sylvain Meignen (LJK, DAO), K\'evin Polisano (LJK, SVH), Micka\"el Nahon (LJK)

item.title: OpenPA: Forced-alignment-free Multi-granular Pronunciation Assessment with Mixed-transcript Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2610.13826v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in automatic pronunciation assessment (APA) have driven a shift from scripted to free-form assessment. However, existing methods often rely on multi-stage pipelines with forced alignment and separate feature extractors, limiting their practicality across response settings. In light of this, we propose OpenPA, a novel APA framework that leverages Whisper's cross-attention mechanism to jointly predict word- and utterance-level pronunciation scores without forced alignment. Through mixed-transcript adaptation and adaptive substitution weighting, OpenPA accommodates heterogeneous transcripts across closed- and open-response settings within a single model. Trained solely on speechocean762, OpenPA achieves the strongest overall performance among evaluated systems under in-domain closed and simulated open-response conditions, while maintaining its performance zero-shot on MultiPA. An additional cross-task evaluation on oral-cancer speech suggests its potential applicability beyond non-native speech.
item.dc:creator: Fu-An Chao, Bi-Cheng Yan, Berlin Chen

item.title: A Multi-Scenario UAV RF Dataset with Real-World Acquisition and Signal Processing Benchmarking
item.description: arXiv:2603.00106v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a real-world multi-scenario unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) radio frequency (RF) dataset, namely DRFF-R2, which is collected using a dedicated acquisition platform under diverse operational conditions. All signals are acquired within a unified framework to ensure consistency in hardware configuration and environmental settings. The dataset is systematically organized into seven well-defined subsets corresponding to different operational and signal composition scenarios to facilitate structured experimentation. Each file follows a clearly annotated naming convention to enable convenient data indexing and reproducible analysis. The dataset contains RF recordings from 26 UAV units spanning 8 distinct models, captured across varying flight states, altitudes, speeds, acquisition days, and receiver configurations. By covering diverse acquisition settings and signal compositions, the dataset provides a comprehensive resource for future UAV RF signal research, including RF fingerprinting (RFF) identification, model-level recognition, flight state analysis, time-varying RFF study, and interference-aware signal processing.
item.dc:creator: Haolin Zheng, Ning Gao, Zhenghang Zhu, Zhijun Huang, Shi Jin, Michail Matthaiou

item.title: Cramer-Rao Bound Analysis of Bistatic ISAC Under Partial Symbol Knowledge and Clutter
item.description: arXiv:2604.11426v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems rely on communication waveforms to perform sensing tasks, thus making their sensing performance strongly dependent on the level of communication symbol knowledge available to the sensing receivers. However, the existing literature fails to capture this dependency, often relying on assumptions of full symbol knowledge. In this paper, we present a Cramer Rao bound (CRB) analysis of a bistatic ISAC network with heterogeneous uplink and downlink illumination and structured clutter. We consider different symbol knowledge regimes by modeling unknown communication symbols as nuisance parameters. Assuming a temporal evolution of the communication channel, we derive a correlation aware channel estimator and an expression for the UEs uplink spectral efficiency. Numerical results show the CRB degradation induced by clutter and symbol uncertainty and how this can affect resource allocation policies. We also show the performance gain of our channel estimator over conventional block fading architectures.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rivetti, Gabor Fodor, Emil Bjornson, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Dynamic Heartbeat Modeling with Recurrent Neural Networks and Inverse Gaussian Point Process
item.description: arXiv:2604.13815v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) analysis is important for the assessment of autonomic cardiovascular regulation. The inverse Gaussian process (IGP) has been widely used for beat-to-beat HRV modeling. However, dynamic estimation of the IGP parameters remains a critical challenge. Conventional parametric approaches such as autoregressive models might be insufficient to capture the nonlinear characteristics of R-R series. In this study, we investigated whether recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can be used for IGP parameter identification and thereby enhance probabilistic modeling of R-R dynamics. Four representative RNN architectures, namely, GRU, LSTM, Structured State Space sequence model (S4), and Mamba, were compared and evaluated using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics. The results demonstrate the possibility of combining RNN with the IGP for beat-wise R-R series modeling. This approach provides a flexible basis for probabilistic HRV modeling and for future incorporation of more complex physiological mechanisms and dynamic conditions.
item.dc:creator: Runwei Lin, Ying Wang

item.title: Edge-Assisted Multimodal UAV Localization with Resource-Efficient Compression and Robust Fusion
item.description: arXiv:2607.03111v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) will play an important role in the future urban transportation systems. This requires designing robust localization schemes especially for non-cooperative UAVs that do not share any information about their movements. This paper designs a multimodal UAV localization framework which utilizes camera, LiDAR and radar sensing modalities. The underlying data processing and the subsequent inference of the UAV location are distributed among the sensing nodes and the edge server attached to the base station. The proposed UAV localization framework addresses three key challenges. First, the sensing nodes have limited computing and communication resources, and they contain only single modality sensors. Second, the multimodal data differ greatly in the sampling rates, time alignment and the encodings. Third, the changes in the environment and the hardware failures cause the modal data to degrade, or to be completely missing. The proposed localization framework utilizes several data processing modules including a information-bottleneck (IB)-based compression module that extracts the most relevant features from each modality, a time-encoding alignment module that provides the unified representation in a shared latent space, a multimodal fusion module that accounts for the degraded and missing data, and a Mamba-based regression module that predicts the present UAV location. The experiments involving a real-world dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately and reliably obtains the UAV location while outperforming other existing frameworks.
item.dc:creator: Zhong Ye, Yinghui He, Guanding Yu, Pavel Loskot

item.title: Input-Correlated Supervision Noise Limits the Benefits of OTA Training for Learned Receivers
item.description: arXiv:2608.12918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While learned wireless receivers are typically studied using synthetic data, the impact of over-the-air (OTA) measurements for training remains unclear. We conducted a 5.88 GHz measurement campaign with a 5G/6G-like orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system across diverse environments and mobility conditions, and trained a neural channel estimator and a capacity-matched end-to-end neural receiver using mixtures of measured and synthetic data. Increasing the OTA fraction revealed a fundamental asymmetry: measured data consistently improved the end-to-end receiver, whereas the channel estimator peaked at an intermediate fraction and degraded with fully measured training. We identified supervision quality as a key contributor: OTA channel labels are derived from noisy received signals and therefore contain supervision errors correlated with the receiver input, whereas decoded bits validated by a cyclic redundancy check (CRC) provide effectively error-free supervision. Denoising the channel labels mitigated the degradation, and a controlled simulation showed that label noise of equal power degrades the estimator far more when it is correlated with the input. For OTA training, end-to-end receivers thus benefit from fully measured data, whereas channel estimators benefit from moderate OTA fractions but require improved label quality.
item.dc:creator: Riku Luostari, Dani Korpi, Olav Tirkkonen, Harri Holma

item.title: One-Bin Fourier Challenges for Dimension-Free Reconstruction Certification
item.description: arXiv:2609.25019v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Partial-Fourier measurement underlies computational imaging, and its reconstructions increasingly come from iterative or learned solvers whose recovery guarantees are conditional on a signal model, a sampling law, and solver accuracy. None of those guarantees transfers to a particular committed output: it can satisfy every acquired coefficient while remaining badly wrong in the unmeasured nullspace. Native Fourier holdout does not repair this, since a spectrally concentrated error is missed unless its bin is drawn, so uniform worst-case risk needs a number of hidden bins proportional to the dimension. We propose a post-commit acceptance test: secret finite-phase masks turn one fixed Fourier readout into dense randomized residual checks, and a median-of-means threshold handles calibrated readout noise. We prove that errors above $E_{\rm rej}$ are rejected and errors below $E_{\rm acc}$ are accepted with confidence $1-\delta$ once $q\ge C(1+N\sigma^2/E_{\rm rej})^2\log(1/\delta)$, explicitly exposing the one-bin resolution floor $N\sigma^2/\sqrt q$; in the zero-noise limit, QPSK gives $4^{-q}$ soundness versus $97.9\%$ minimax false acceptance for a worst-case ordinary-bin error. At a fixed noise-to-threshold ratio, measured screening false acceptance fell from about $21\%$ at 16 checks to $5\%$ at 64; a data-consistent learned nullspace failure with NMSE $0.200$ was rejected by $96.9\%$ of challenge banks while 16 ordinary bins missed it $98.9\%$ of the time; and error statistics at 16 checks stayed stable from 128 through $65{,}536$ dimensions. The test supports solver acceptance, model selection, and stopping certification, with a certified fresh-bank error interval.
item.dc:creator: Milad Bafarassat

item.title: DeltaLLM: Delta-Key Sparse Attention for Edge LLMs
item.description: arXiv:2507.19608v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On-device LLM inference is increasingly important for edge platforms but remains challenging due to high computational and memory demands and tight resource constraints. Modern applications often involve long prompts. Although compact models reduce linear-layer costs through weight compression, attention remains largely unoptimized and becomes the dominant bottleneck, especially during prefilling. Existing attention pruning methods primarily target highly parallel hardware (e.g., GPUs) and long context windows, limiting their suitability for edge scenarios. We present DeltaLLM, a training-free LLM framework based on algorithm-hardware-dataflow co-design to accelerate prefilling attention. DeltaLLM introduces a causal-attention-aware K-only delta formulation that enables Delta-Key reuse across query heads under Grouped-Query Attention (GQA). A context-aware hybrid strategy preserves exact attention near the diagonal while applying delta approximation to nonlocal regions. For score-value multiplication, we propose a vectorized structured sparse online softmax (VSSOS) that converts fine-grained spatial score sparsity into hardware-friendly column-level skipping. A specialized vector-processor architecture and unified sparse/dense attention dataflow exploit the resulting sparsity. Evaluated on BitNet-b1.58-2B-4T and LLaMA3.2-1B-Instruct, DeltaLLM achieves up to 60% Delta-Key sparsity and 63% structured attention-score sparsity with negligible average accuracy loss. On the KV260 FPGA board, it delivers a 1.62x speedup over TeLLMe-v2 while reducing DSP and BRAM usage. These results show that DeltaLLM supports efficient edge LLM deployment and integration with existing pipelines without fine-tuning.
item.dc:creator: Jiawen Qi, Jiayu Liu, Chang Gao, Zhaochun Ren, Qinyu Chen

item.title: Integer-Forcing Precoding: A Geometric Perspective and Low-Complexity Algorithm Design
item.description: arXiv:2602.20529v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The joint coefficient--scaling design of integer-forcing (IF) precoding couples a full-rank integer coefficient matrix with a positive diagonal scaling matrix, resulting in a mixed discrete--continuous optimization problem. We first distinguish the original full-rank formulation and its finite-field invertibility requirement from the unimodular restriction studied in the subsequent analysis. Under this restriction, we formulate coefficient selection as the unimodular minimum-sum basis problem (UMSBP). By parameterizing the scaling matrix with its normalized diagonal vector, we define a deterministic exact single-output UMSBP oracle whose preimages partition the scaling manifold into disjoint coefficient-labelled regions. The restricted objective is consequently represented as the lower envelope of fixed-coefficient quadratic functions. Based on this formulation, we derive an exact decomposition into fixed-coefficient scaling optimization, coefficient-consistency verification, cross-region exploration, and candidate comparison. We prove that exact UMSBP evaluation is NP-hard through a polynomial-time reduction from exact Euclidean CVP. For a fixed coefficient matrix, we derive an equivalent convex formulation, its normalized stationarity condition, and a matrix-balancing interpretation. Under the stated positivity and finite-projective-diameter condition
item.dc:creator: Junren Qin, Fan Jiang, Tao Yang, Shanxiang Lyu, Rongke Liu, Shi Jin

item.title: Mode 0: Architecture, Risk Taxonomy, and Standardization Pathway for RCU-Assisted V2X Safety Communication
item.description: arXiv:2605.25431v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The 3GPP V2X resource allocation framework offers two entity classes for coordinating vehicle communication --- base-station scheduling and autonomous vehicle selection --- a design space we show to be structurally incomplete for safety-critical coordination. We propose Mode 0, a third entity class centered on the Roadside Computing Unit (RCU): infrastructure integrating elevated sensing, sidelink communication, and local computation, owned by traffic management authorities rather than network operators. We formalize Mode 0's subfamily taxonomy (Mode 0a through 0c), its traffic risk taxonomy and mandatory-escalation boundary, its cross-domain coexistence with Modes 1--4, and its standardization pathway. Of the three failure modes motivating this proposal --- scheduling saturation, occlusion-driven information gaps, and an institutional authority gap during severe hazards --- only scheduling is evaluated by simulation; information and authority are argued architecturally and evidenced by independent deployment convergence across Chinese local and industry-alliance standards, Chinese operator infrastructure, and European and US C-V2X programs, properties no channel-level simulation can instantiate. In a multi-agent reinforcement learning simulation (88 training runs, 95% confidence intervals), per-vehicle policies (Mode 0c) raise worst-interval delivery reliability at the critical safety load from 0.217 under shared per-class policies (Mode 0a) to 0.792, cutting lost safety messages from 38% to 6%. An idealized model of standardized sensing-based semi-persistent scheduling loses 10% at the same load, and per-vehicle coordination more than halves the longest gaps between safety updates against it (3.9 against 8.4 message periods). With spare spectrum, a safety partition sized by the RCU delivers every safety message. We call for a 3GPP study item to formalize Mode 0.
item.dc:creator: Dewei Jiang (Nantong University), Xiang Gu (Nantong University)

item.title: Fundamental Limits of Quantized MIMO ISAC under Gaussian Signaling
item.description: arXiv:2606.31301v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a quantized multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system in which the communication and sensing receivers each apply analog spatial combining followed by scalar subtractive dithered quantization. This quantization model leads to an additive effective-noise representation with non-Gaussian noise. We derive upper and lower bounds on the capacity of this channel. Numerical results show that these bounds are tight at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and saturate at high SNR due to finite-resolution quantization. They also show that, despite the effective noise being non-Gaussian, independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) isotropic Gaussian signaling achieves rates close to capacity. Focusing on i.i.d. Gaussian signaling, this paper also presents a closed-form expression for the linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE) achieved under a Kronecker sensing-channel model. Numerical results show that the LMMSE also saturates at high SNR, where the saturation level increases as the spatial combining ratio decreases, and for combining ratios below one, saturation occurs even without quantization.
item.dc:creator: Hossein Atrsaei, Mireille Sarkiss, Mich\`ele Wigger

item.title: Mean Gain Is Not a Guarantee: Risk-Controlled Open-Loop Scheduling for Ka-Band LEO Semantic Downlinks
item.description: arXiv:2608.08635v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A low-Earth-orbit satellite has only minutes to downlink imagery on a limited power budget, and some moments in a pass carry far better channels than others. Spending more power on the good moments and skipping hopeless ones should deliver more images, but the channel cannot be measured in time, so the schedule is planned in advance from weather statistics using a safety margin. That margin is sized so the forecast is statistically reliable, and the scheduler is judged by whether it beats uniform power on average. Both targets are wrong for a satellite that gets one attempt per pass: on real Sentinel-2 imagery, a scheduler gaining one to two images per pass on average still delivers fewer than uniform power on a quarter to a third of individual passes, and a genie knowing the weather exactly does no better. We instead size the margin by measuring, on recorded passes, how often it would have backfired, keeping only settings that provably backfire rarely. The procedure declines to schedule our learned codec and certifies scheduling for codecs with a sharper cliff.
item.dc:creator: Milad Bafarassat

item.title: Compressibility is not Feedback: A Random-access Gap in Causal Semantic Repair
item.description: arXiv:2609.25020v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Semantic feedback can repair a noisy first decode without retransmitting the whole message, but current end-to-end evaluations hide where a feedback design fails. An oracle that sees both the source-side state and receiver observation may describe a useful correction with few bits, while the receiver, which sees only its own observation, may not know which correction to request. We formulate these as distinct direct and receiver-constrained coding problems, connect repair distortion to retained local utility and prove a random-access separation: one direct bit is exact although receiver utility vanishes with the number of source-conditioned alternatives. A synthetic ladder verifies the exact law. In paired populations of eight Reuters text-JSCC codecs, the trained recurrent population retains over three times more direct 16-bit repair value than the trained DeepSC population despite comparable full-repair opportunity. Nevertheless, an entropy-valid receiver audit across all eight recurrent checkpoints does not resolve against repetition, source-only or shuffled-index controls. The results show that compressible repair is an upper bound, not evidence of deployable feedback, and motivate reporting both rate curves under matched resources.
item.dc:creator: Milad Bafarassat

item.title: ThinkNet: Evolutionary Deep Ensembles for Efficient Motor-Imagery EEG Classification
item.description: arXiv:2609.33967v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Practical assistive and rehabilitative brain--computer interfaces require subject-independent motor-imagery EEG (MI-EEG) decoders that generalize to new users under limited target-user data and constrained compute. However, held-out-subject performance can be overstated when test-subject information influences preprocessing, model selection, or ensemble selection. We present \textit{ThinkNet}, a validation-controlled framework that combines train-only normalization, validation-guided evolutionary search, and validation-gated inference to identify compact decoders and inference policies for held-out subjects. We evaluate four-class BCI Competition IV-2a (session T) decoding with nine Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) folds, three seeds, seven fixed decoder entries, and a broader search over ten representative decoder families; the held-out subject is never used for normalization, hyperparameter, architecture, or ensemble-policy selection. In the fixed benchmark, the validation-selected compact decoder achieved 44.35$\pm$15.41\% accuracy with 4.9K parameters, 19 KB FP32 weights, and 0.99 ms batch-1 Orin CUDA inference. Across the broader search, compact models ($\leq$25K parameters) achieved higher mean held-out accuracy than mid-size and large alternatives after selected retraining (40.10\% vs. 35.09\% and 34.78\%). Validation-gated ensembling improved over validation-selected single-model inference, reaching 43.98$\pm$16.25\% in the fixed benchmark and 43.31$\pm$15.88\% for the compact six-family ensemble. A non-deployable oracle analysis revealed a 6.1-point family-selection gap and near-zero validation--test correlation, showing that validation reliability remains a key bottleneck under subject shift. Thus, ThinkNet is a validation-controlled framework for compact MI-EEG model and inference-policy selection, rather than a single-architecture benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Abdul Basit, Saim Rehman, Muhammad Shafique

item.title: Memory- and Bandwidth-Efficient SPAD-LiDAR Ranging via Coarse-to-Fine Spline Sketching
item.description: arXiv:2609.35126v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work presents an optimized compression framework for direct time-of-flight (dToF) light detection and ranging (LiDAR), using an accurate, compact timestamp-encoding strategy to address the high data-rate bottleneck from single-photon timing information in single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays. We propose a hardware-friendly timestamp-to-depth framework in which a sparse single-photon encoding strategy, namely coarse-to-fine spline sketches (CFSS), projects photon timestamps into fine-grained, low-dimensional representations, called sketch values. CFSS converts timestamps on-the-fly to sketch values and accumulates them with lower memory consumption, without constructing histograms, thereby saving on-chip/device memory. CFSS's closed-form solution for ToF retrieval ensures iteration-free reconstruction. Compared with the conventional sketched-LiDAR framework, the proposed method retains the same compression ratio in the single-peak case, ranging from hundreds$\times$ to thousands$\times$ depending on the accuracy-complexity trade-off, while improving depth-estimation accuracy. Both synthetic and real datasets are used to validate the performance. The CFSS framework is further extended to two-peak scenarios, enabling recovery of objects obscured by partially occluding camouflage and uniformly scattering semi-transparent media. Firmware implementation is also investigated by clearly separating online hardware processing from offline software workloads.
item.dc:creator: Zhenya Zang, Istvan Gyongy, Mike Davies
